title: Distinct Difference Array
description:
# Distinct Difference Array

Given a zero-indexed integer array `nums`, build an array `diff` of the same length. For each index `i`, `diff[i]` is the number of distinct values in the prefix `nums[0..i]` minus the number of distinct values in the suffix `nums[i+1..n-1]`.

The suffix after the last index is empty, so it has `0` distinct values. Values may be negative or very large; equality of values is the only thing that matters.

## Example 1:

**Input:** nums = [1,2,3,4,5]
**Output:** [-3,-1,1,3,5]

## Example 2:

**Input:** nums = [3,2,3,4,2]
**Output:** [-2,-1,0,2,3]

## Constraints:

*   `1 <= nums.length <= 10^5`
*   `-10^9 <= nums[i] <= 10^9`

solutions.name: Prefix and Suffix Distinct Arrays
solutions.description:
## Approach

Scan from right to left and store `suffixDistinct[i]`, the number of distinct values in `nums[i..n-1]`. Then scan from left to right with a prefix set and compute `prefix.size() - suffixDistinct[i + 1]` for every cut.

## Key Insight

The suffix in the formula starts after index `i`, so the precomputed value must be read from `i + 1`. Keeping a sentinel slot at `n` naturally represents the empty suffix as zero.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(n)

solutions.name: Rolling Suffix Frequency Map
solutions.description:
## Approach

Count all values in a suffix frequency map first. Move the cut from left to right: add the current value to the prefix set, remove one copy from the suffix map, and subtract the live suffix distinct count.

## Key Insight

A value stops contributing to the suffix only when its remaining frequency becomes zero. Tracking that count directly avoids building a separate suffix array.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(n)

solutions.name: First and Last Occurrence Sweep
solutions.description:
## Approach

Record the first and last index of every value. A value increases the prefix distinct count at its first index, and it contributes to the suffix count for exactly the cuts before its last index. Sweep those boundary events to build the answer.

## Key Insight

The formula depends only on whether a value has appeared on the left and whether it will appear again on the right. First and last occurrences encode those two facts without maintaining live sets during the final sweep.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(n)

solutions.name: Coordinate Compression Counts
solutions.description:
## Approach

Sort a copy of `nums` to assign each distinct value a compact id. Use two count arrays, one for values already seen on the left and one for values still present on the right, then update both distinct counters as the cut moves.

## Key Insight

Hash maps are not required if arbitrary integer values are first compressed into the range `0..d-1`. The same rolling-frequency idea then becomes simple array indexing.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n log n)
- Space Complexity: O(n)
